Emily / Monica / team —

Quick technical summary to address the RFP controls list. Below are the key items and where you can find evidence:

Encryption:
- Data in transit: TLS 1.2+ for all client-service and inter-service traffic.
- Data at rest: AES-256 with per-tenant keys managed via customer KMS integration (supports AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / customer HSM).

Access controls & separation:
- RBAC + attribute-based gating for PHI access; least privilege enforced at runtime.
- KV cache (model context) is namespace-isolated per customer and scrubbed after task completion unless caching is explicitly enabled per app.

KV / Cache and PHI handling:
- We support configurable prefix/KV caching. PHI can be marked non-cacheable at the API level; default policy for healthcare customers is no persistent KV caching of PHI.

Auditability & logging:
- Per-request immutable audit logs with request/response hashes, actor ID, model variant, and timestamps.
- We can provide a redacted sample audit-log CSV for inspection (attached).

Data residency & deletion:
- Support regional pinning of compute and storage.
- Deletion workflows: immediate soft-delete + secure wipe after retention window; manual data purge options available.

BAA & evidence:
- We operate under a BAA for covered engagements; we provided a standard template.
- SOC2 Type II available (summary attached); full report under NDA.

Pen tests & vulnerability mgmt:
- Quarterly third-party penetration tests; yearly large-scale cloud security assessments.

Attachments included in this message: phi-dataflow-mapping.xlsx; network-diagram.png; audit-log-sample.csv

If you want a short technical walkthrough (30 min) I can take your security or engineering team through the above and share the live diagrams.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
